context.question: Whether the sick would live or die, and what his disease was?
context.asked_at: 16 July 1645 (figure heading; see the ocr_note on the year).
context.setting: A sickness question on the figure of 16 July 1645.

attachments.key_positions: The Ascendant most afflicted by the corporal presence of a planet who is partly lord of the eighth house; the sign of the sixth fixed and afflicted, and the lord of the sixth in a fixed, earthly, melancholy sign; the Sun, the temporal light, in perfect opposition of Saturn, lord of the sixth, in fixed signs; the Moon neer the Dragon's Tail (Cauda Leonis in the OCR) and afflicted in the Ascendant
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment; the ascending sign's glyph is corrupt in the OCR and is not asserted here.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. XLVI: whether the sick would live or die, and what his disease was (figure of 16 July 1645)
provenance.version: 1647 first edition (Internet Archive scan OCR, auxiliary/christian-astrology-vol1-3_djvu.txt); wording cross-checked against the 1852 Zadkiel edition (Introduction to Astrology) and the second OCR (christian-astrology-1647-original_djvu.txt) where noted
